0.long_answer: Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPSs) are classified as lysosomal storage diseases because they result from the deficiency of specific enzymes within lysosomes. These enzymes normally function to break down glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). Lysosomes are versatile organelles involved in a variety of cellular processes including secretion, plasma membrane repair, apoptosis, cell signaling, and even aspects of energy metabolism. When the lysosomal enzymes are deficient, as is the case in MPSs, the normal degradation process is disrupted leading to the accumulation of undegraded substrates, which in turn causes the cellular and tissue dysfunction associated with the disease.
